rows.notes: The study is explicitly a review (title and header 'Review'; abstract: 'Here, we review that progress') of plant physiological and molecular responses to drought. It reports no own data. It does not address drip irrigation at all; the only agricultural mention is that chemical-signalling knowledge has been exploited to regulate water use (citing Davies et al. 2002) and that imaging may aid irrigation scheduling. No evidence on drip irrigation delivering water conservation or improved WUE.

Review article without own data. It does not examine irrigation calendars/scheduling based on soil salinity and water table depth; it only remarks, citing others, that thermal/fluorescence imaging may become useful for field irrigation scheduling and that chemical-signalling-based control (partial root-zone drying, Davies et al. 2002) has improved regulation of water use. No own result on scheduling-based water conservation.

notes: Chaves et al. (2003) is a narrative review in Functional Plant Biology on plant responses to drought from genes to whole plant. It contains no primary data and does not discuss drip irrigation, salinity/water-table-based irrigation calendars, or wastewater reuse; the reviewing paper's attribution of agricultural WUE improvements from these techniques to this source is not supported by its content. Full text appears complete (pp. 239-264 including references).
